C1.statement: The pool is a golang universal network connection pool.
C1.fragment: A golang universal network connection pool.

C2.statement: The connection type in the connection pool is interface{}, making it more versatile.
C2.fragment: The connection type in the connection pool is `interface{}`

C3.statement: The connection supports setting the maximum idle time.
C3.fragment: The connection supports setting the maximum idle time

C4.statement: A timeout connection will be closed and discarded.
C4.fragment: the timeout connection will be closed and discarded

C5.statement: Setting maximum idle time can avoid the problem of automatic connection failure when idle.

C8.statement: The pool supports connection waiting when the connection pool is full (like the go db connection pool).

C9.statement: factory specifies the method to create the connection.
C9.fragment: //factory Specify the method to create the connection

C10.statement: close specifies the method to close the connection.
C10.fragment: //close Specify the method to close the connection

C11.statement: ping specifies the method to detect whether the connection is invalid.

C12.statement: InitialCap configures the initial number of connections (5 in the example).
C12.fragment: Initialize the number of connections to 5

C13.statement: MaxIdle configures the maximum idle connection (20 in the example).

C14.statement: MaxCap configures the maximum concurrent connection (30 in the example).

C15.statement: IdleTimeout configures the maximum idle time of the connection; a connection exceeding this time will be closed.
C15.fragment: The maximum idle time of the connection, the connection exceeding this time will be closed

C16.statement: The idle timeout can avoid the problem of automatic failure when connecting to EOF when idle.

C19.fragment: //Put the connection back into the connection pool, when the connection is no longer in use

C20.statement: p.Release releases all connections in the connection pool when resources need to be destroyed.
C20.fragment: //Release all connections in the connection pool, when resources need to be destroyed

questions: Is the pool an ordering when NewChannelPool initializes InitialCap connections—does it create them at construction time?
What happens on Get when the pool is full and connection waiting is supported—does Get block, and for how long or with what timeout?
When is the ping method invoked—on Get, on Put, periodically, or elsewhere?
What happens when Factory returns an error during initialization or on Get?
What happens when Close returns an error during Release or idle-timeout discard?
Is InitialCap bounded by MaxIdle or MaxCap, and what happens if InitialCap exceeds either?
How does MaxIdle interact with MaxCap—what happens when idle connections exceed MaxIdle but total is below MaxCap?
Is Len counting idle connections, total connections, or checked-out connections?
Does Release wait for checked-out connections to be Put back, or close everything immediately?
What happens to a connection Put back after Release was called?
What error does Get return and when (e.g., pool exhausted, factory error)?
Is the IdleTimeout measured from creation, from last Put, or from last use?
Are idle connections proactively swept at IdleTimeout, or only checked lazily on Get?
When a ping check fails, is the invalid connection closed via the Close function before being discarded?
Does Get validate a connection with ping before returning it, and if invalid, does it create a new one?
Does Put validate the connection (e.g., via ping) before returning it to the pool?
Is the zero value of Config valid, and what defaults apply for unspecified parameters?
